scope: Read-only public-play audit of Jurassic World Evolution 3 operational granularity, translated into a reviewable CHOOGuard interaction contract

verdict.operatingUnit: The strongest public evidence makes an operational team/vehicle the manually selected work unit. A facility owns or provides teams; a selected team receives a direct task, or is assigned to a post/camera patrol that automatically reacts within range.
verdict.visibleActors: Many visible actors do not imply one player command surface per rendered object. Public guides distinguish guests, dinosaurs, operational teams/vehicles, and staff/scientists by different management verbs.
verdict.microControlBoundary: Direct vehicle control exists as a separate optional mode. It does not prove that normal management play requires driving each vehicle or selecting each crew body.
verdict.unknownBoundary: The public guides do not establish whether an operational vehicle and its crew are separate internal entities. They establish only the player-facing team/vehicle task surface.
verdict.chooguardConsequence: Use facility-owned response groups or teams as selectable command units, then issue tasks to incident or area targets. Do not make each visible vehicle, crew body, or visitor a required controller row.

revokedProposals: The earlier proposal to require independent selection of every vehicle/crew is withdrawn.
The earlier eight-row per-vehicle controller is only an unimplemented proposal and is withdrawn from the interaction contract.
WASD may remain an optional shortcut, but it cannot be required for the primary operation path.
Earlier pending camera/fleet proposal questions are superseded by this evidence graph.

failedReadOnlyAttempt.effect: No claim was derived from the failed request; the dated local official cache is used instead.

exactTextBudget.text: Response Facility to access Ranger and Capture Teams
automatically complete any relevant tasks from this Maintenance Post

lineEvidence.fact: A Maintenance ATV Team can be assigned to a Maintenance Post; inner and outer radii govern different automatic coverage.
Maintenance work has two public paths: a direct task on a selected team, or automatic work through a post assignment.
Ranger Teams use Response Facility supplies, can receive task assignment, and can automate status checks and feeder work through a Ranger Post.
Capture Teams come from Response Facilities and can tranquilise through a direct task or an automatic security-camera patrol response.
Building a Response Facility is the documented way to access Ranger and Capture Teams; placement distance affects travel to targets.

exactTextBudget.text: drive ground-based vehicles by taking direct control
All park teams carry a camera

lineEvidence.fact: ATVs, MVUs, Ranger Vehicles, and helicopters can enter direct-control mode; the player can exit back to the normal camera.
Vehicle-specific tools are available in direct control, including capture-team dart actions.
Capture Teams may be assigned for automatic protection in range, while damaged vehicles return to a base of operation.
The guide speaks of park teams and team vehicles together, including a camera used while controlling a team vehicle.

exactTextBudget.text: Ranger Teams can be assigned to Ranger Posts.
automatically carry out Status Checks on dinosaurs within range

lineEvidence.fact: A powered Security Camera with a Capture Team patrol automatically detects a threatening dinosaur in range and calls the team.
Ranger, MVU, and Capture teams can be assigned to a Ranger Post for different automatic monitoring work around that post.

exactTextBudget.text: Guests are grouped together by their interests
control the split of groups at specific locations

lineEvidence.fact: Guests are managed as demographic groups whose distribution is influenced by species, enclosure design, and attraction placement.
Guest safety is managed through park conditions, Capture Teams, and shelters; the guide does not describe direct per-guest commands.

exactTextBudget.text: Teams can be assigned to automatically deal with dinosaur escapes, broken fences or sick animals

lineEvidence.fact: The manager delegates day-to-day operations to staffed facilities and automatically assigned teams.
Security-camera detection alerts a Capture Team, after which a Maintenance Team can be sent to repair the escape point.

exactTextBudget.text: Vehicle Task Assignment / Next Vehicle / Previous Vehicle

lineEvidence.fact: The cached keyboard table lists camera movement, zoom, and rotation keys. It does not preserve a mouse-wheel binding.
Shortcuts navigate to the nearest Response, Paleo-Medical, or Maintenance facility.
The public control surface calls the task context Vehicle Task Assignment and provides next/previous vehicle navigation.
Ranger/wheeled vehicles and Capture Teams have separate direct-control bindings, reinforcing direct driving as a distinct mode.

exactTextBudget.text: fleet of vehicles that you can call on

lineEvidence.fact: The player is framed as a park manager who manages a workforce and calls on a vehicle fleet to run operations.

exactTextBudget.text: Maintenance Posts to automate Repair, Reboot, Resupply and Inspection tasks

lineEvidence.fact: Maintenance Facilities own assignable ATV Teams; Maintenance Posts automate coverage by inner and outer radii.
Team resources live at respective facilities and may be restocked directly at a building or through Maintenance Patrol automation.

publicInteractionStatechart.mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Overview
  Overview --> FacilityContext: select Response/Maintenance/Paleo-Medical facility
  FacilityContext --> TeamSelected: choose team/vehicle
  TeamSelected --> DirectTask: Add Task + choose eligible work/target
  DirectTask --> AssignedWork: accept assignment
  AssignedWork --> TravelAndAct: team uses facility resources and performs work
  TravelAndAct --> FacilityContext: task complete / returns or awaits next work
  TeamSelected --> PatrolAssigned: assign to Maintenance Post, Ranger Post, or Security Camera patrol
  PatrolAssigned --> AutomaticCoverage: facility/post/camera monitors supported events in range
  AutomaticCoverage --> TravelAndAct: matching event triggers team response
  TeamSelected --> DirectControl: optional take direct control of team vehicle
  DirectControl --> Overview: back out to normal camera
limits: The guides prove assignment and automatic response, but do not document a visible multi-task queue depth or reorder UI.
The guides use both team and vehicle language; they do not prove a separate selectable on-foot crew-body layer.
The cached official controls prove keyboard zoom and vehicle cycling, but not an exact mouse-wheel binding.

actorClassifications.directFact: Public guidance manages guests through demographics, park layout, attractions, comfort, transport, shelter coverage, and site-wide or local shelter operation.
actorClassifications.playerControlClaim: No direct per-guest command is documented in the inspected public guides.
actorClassifications.inferenceGuard: Do not claim guests are one AI, many independent AIs, or non-selectable internal GameObjects; only the player-facing management surface is evidenced.

actorClassifications.directFact: Dinosaurs are scanned, treated, tranquilised, transported, photographed, wrangled, or commanded with Send/Summon through relevant team and vehicle tools.
actorClassifications.playerControlClaim: They are eligible task targets and can receive limited behavior commands from a vehicle; this is not evidence that they share guest behavior or operational-unit ownership.

actorClassifications.directFact: A team/vehicle can be selected in its facility or in the park, assigned a direct task or patrol, and optionally driven in a separate direct-control mode.
actorClassifications.playerControlClaim: This is the evidenced operational command unit.

actorClassifications.directFact: The guides describe teams, team vehicles, facilities, supplies, scientists, and staff, but do not document selecting an individual embodied crew member for field movement.
actorClassifications.playerControlClaim: Treat an on-screen crew body as presentation unless another primary source or product requirement grants it a command surface.
actorClassifications.inferenceGuard: Do not claim the crew body is or is not a separate simulation entity.

actorClassifications.directFact: Scientists are assigned to research and expedition tasks through management interfaces; Staff Centres manage capacity, rest, and training.
actorClassifications.playerControlClaim: The inspected guides evidence roster/task assignment, not direct embodied movement.

mouseFirstOperationRecipe.principle: The cursor selects a command context and group-owned unit; the wheel navigates scale; clicks compose facility/team, task, and target. Keyboard shortcuts remain optional accelerators.

steps.interaction: Move the cursor over the world and use the mouse wheel to zoom to the facility or incident.
steps.evidenceStatus: user_required_and_current_code_supported; exact JWE3 wheel binding unverified
support: JWE3_CONTROLS lines 123-135 proves zoom as a camera action but only preserves keyboard bindings

steps.interaction: Left-click a Response, Maintenance, or Paleo-Medical facility to open its owned operational groups; alternatively click an incident to see eligible groups.
steps.evidenceStatus: source-grounded information architecture; exact click gesture is a CHOOGuard translation

steps.interaction: Left-click one team/vehicle group, then click Add Task or Assign Patrol. Do not require selecting every rendered vehicle or crew body.
steps.evidenceStatus: directly_supported unit and command verbs; grouping multiple visible members under one CHOOGuard row is a product inference

steps.interaction: For a direct task, click an eligible incident, infrastructure item, dinosaur, or area target. For automation, click a post/camera and confirm the coverage assignment.
steps.evidenceStatus: direct-task and range-automation distinction directly supported; CHOOGuard target taxonomy requires design review

steps.interaction: Show one accepted assignment on the group card, travel/work state, and automatic coverage radius. Further task queuing is optional product behavior and must not be presented as proven JWE3 semantics.
steps.evidenceStatus: assignment and automatic work directly supported; visible queue behavior insufficient

steps.interaction: Offer Direct Control as a secondary action on supported operational vehicles, with an explicit return to overview.

optionalAccelerators: WASD or arrow-key pan may remain available, but no required task step depends on them.
Facility and next/previous vehicle shortcuts may be added as optional accelerators after the pointer path works.

files.current: Wheel zoom and middle-button drag pan exist; WASD/arrows and Q/E also control the camera.
files.gap: The primary operation path is not yet specified and validated as mouse-first; WASD must be an optional shortcut rather than a prerequisite.

files.current: The workspace exposes three abstract team buttons: operations, fire, and medical; actions and targets are fixed to move/hold and platform/concourse/exit plus crowd controls.
files.gap: There is no facility-owned roster, Add Task flow, incident eligibility panel, patrol/post assignment, or coverage-radius feedback.

files.current: The agency panel contains exactly two request/return/tracking rows, one for fire and one for medical.
files.gap: No eight-row vehicle controller exists. The panel groups by two fixed support-team IDs but does not express facility ownership or group capacity.

files.current: Queues are keyed by selected logical team. Left-click selects one of three team markers or a crowd cohort; right-click chooses a hard-coded destination or triggers cohort release.
files.gap: The world click contract is coupled to team markers and fixed station targets, rather than facility/team ownership, eligible incident targets, and area automation.

files.current: The local synthetic port stores three logical teams and validates exactly one team, one target, and only move/hold actions.
files.gap: The state model has no facility-to-team ownership, operational-unit category, task capability, incident target, patrol anchor, or coverage assignment.

currentChooguardGap.acceptanceGap: This audit is source and code inspection only. It does not establish runtime usability, Unity scene behavior, or product acceptance.

directFactsVsInferences.claim: Facilities provide operational teams and supplies.
A team/vehicle is selectable for direct task assignment.
A single CHOOGuard response-group row may represent multiple visible vehicles or crew members.
directFactsVsInferences.guard: The public sources do not specify CHOOGuard group size, pooling, or one-to-many rendering.

directFactsVsInferences.claim: Every visible operational vehicle must be independently selectable.
Visible crew bodies and their vehicles are the same internal entity.
Visitors, dinosaurs, response vehicles, and crew bodies share one AI or one selection model.
JWE3 publicly documents mouse-wheel zoom and exact left-click task composition.
directFactsVsInferences.guard: Use mouse wheel and left click as the explicit CHOOGuard product requirement, not as a falsely attributed exact JWE3 binding.

reviewGate.next: Jev independent review of source-to-claim fidelity, actor boundaries, and the mouse-first CHOOGuard translation
reviewGate.then: Present the reviewed concrete interaction contract to the user for confirmation
reviewQuestions: Does every directly_supported claim have a matching local line range and no broader wording than the source?
Does the contract keep facility, operational group, rendered vehicle, crew body, guest crowd, and dinosaur distinct?
Does the pointer path avoid requiring selection of every visible object?
Are wheel and click choices labeled as CHOOGuard requirements where exact JWE3 bindings are unverified?
Does the plan avoid presenting the current per-team queue as proven JWE3 behavior?
